```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4, dpi = 96)
```

`fit_models()` treats every model the same way, so a new model only needs a
**spec**: its calibration bounds and a `build()` function. Once registered,
it gets the same forcing, folds, calibration, climate-contrast test,
summaries, plots and `predict()` as the built-in models.

```{r setup}
library(WSVAflowR)
options(wsva.data_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "wsva"))
wsva_models()[["CemaNeige-GR4J"]]
```

## The contract

`build(x, n_layers)` receives the basin's model inputs and returns a
closure `function(params)` that gives daily flow in mm/day, one value per
row of `x$daily`:

* `x$daily`: forcing (`forcing_required_vars()`), plus `tmean_c`, `eto_mm`
  (Penman-Monteith reference ET) and `pet_mm` (ETo × land-cover crop
  coefficient), and observed `q_mm`
* `x$static`: one row of basin attributes (`lat`, `elev_m`, `swc_max_mm`,
  `jtemp_c`, `kc_dormant`, ...)
* `x$hypso`: 101 elevation quantiles, for elevation-band snow models

Do the expensive set-up (anything that does not depend on the parameters)
in `build()`, outside the closure: the closure runs once per calibration
step.

## A small example

A deliberately simple model: a degree-day snowpack feeding one linear
reservoir, with runoff reduced by PET.

```{r spec}
snow_bucket <- wsva_model(
  id = "snowres", name = "Snow + linear reservoir",
  bounds = param_bounds(ddf = c(0.5, 8),     # melt factor (mm/C/day)
                        k = c(2, 200),       # reservoir time constant (days)
                        et = c(0, 1)),       # fraction of PET removed
  build = function(x, n_layers) {
    p_in <- x$daily$prcp_mm; t <- x$daily$tmean_c; pet <- x$daily$pet_mm
    snow_frac <- t < x$static$jtemp_c
    function(par) {
      swe <- 0; water <- numeric(length(p_in))
      for (i in seq_along(p_in)) {
        if (snow_frac[i]) swe <- swe + p_in[i]
        melt <- if (t[i] > 0) min(swe, par$ddf * t[i]) else 0
        swe <- swe - melt
        water[i] <- max((if (snow_frac[i]) 0 else p_in[i]) + melt - par$et * pet[i], 0)
      }
      route_ihacres(water, tau_q = par$k, tau_s = par$k, vs = 0)
    }
  },
  reference = "Vignette example")
register_model(snow_bucket)
```

## Fit it next to a built-in model

```{r fit, fig.alt = "Observed and simulated mean monthly flow for GR4J and the example snow and linear reservoir model"}
b <- example_basin()
fits <- fit_models(b, models = c("gr4j", "snowres"), cv = "blocked", n_evals = 80)
summary(fits)
plot(fits, type = "seasonal")
```

The simple model can be compared with GR4J on exactly the same held-out
years, and `predict(fits, forcing = ...)` runs it with new climate like any
other model.
